title: Global bond sell-off: 30-year UST yields hit highest since 2007, gilts since 1998
content: A fresh global sell-off in long-dated government bonds pushed the 30-year UST yield to around 5.3% this week (17-21 August 2026), the highest since 2007, while the UK 30-year gilt yield climbed to roughly 5.8%, its highest since 1998; German Bunds were also hit. The rout was driven by heavy long-dated debt issuance, persistent above-target inflation and a fresh Middle East oil shock after a ceasefire window lapsed and Gulf shipping came under attack. The US Treasury said it would at least double long-dated debt buybacks to $4bn per operation to steady the market. Equities wobbled as yields rose before a Friday rebound left the S&P 500 higher on the day but lower on the week.

title: Trump declares 'economic warfare' on Iran, Brent jumps near $94 on Hormuz fears
content: US President Trump said on 19 August 2026 that Washington was launching what he called the "most crushing economic operation ever taken against any country" against Iran, with Treasury Secretary Bessent vowing to squeeze Iran's economy and warning any nation aiding Tehran's sanctions evasion would face severe penalties. Brent crude jumped over 2% to close near $94/bbl, having risen more than 3% intraday, as Strait of Hormuz transits fell towards zero and Iranian crude's pricing flipped from a discount to a premium versus Brent. The escalation compounds inflation risks already troubling the Fed, ECB and BoE, and was a key driver of the week's broader government bond sell-off.

title: Fed minutes show most hawkish FOMC split since 2016 as dissent builds for Sept
content: Minutes from the Fed's 28-29 July meeting, released 19 August 2026, confirmed the FOMC voted 9-3 to hold rates at 3.50-3.75%, with three regional presidents (Cleveland, Minneapolis, Dallas) dissenting in favour of a quarter-point hike, the most dissents since September 2016. Minutes showed "many participants" judged further tightening would likely be needed if inflation stayed elevated, with some officials doubting financial conditions were tight enough to return inflation to the 2% target. Market-implied odds of a September hike initially rose before easing on weaker payrolls and softer core inflation, adding to a volatile week for UST yields and the USD ahead of the Fed's Jackson Hole symposium.
